principles: Opt-in / inert by default — the writer is a no-op until a flag enables it
Single writer choke-point: exactly one exported append path so later slices wire through one place
Mirror the spec's record shape exactly (four-field, no totalTokens, per-dimension null)
Reuse the existing runtime-artifact-registry; the ledger path is excluded from materialHash and is volatile/repairable
Foundation only — no provider/estimate/budget/authority wiring in this slice
drivers: Every later ledger slice depends on a correct, tamper-evident, privacy-safe writer foundation
The ledger path must never pollute evidence or gate hashes
Getting the record shape wrong here propagates to every future record

options.name: A: new self-contained core/usage-ledger module + registry entry, opt-in
pros: Easy to extend in later slices
Inert by default = low blast radius

options.name: B: inline writer into an existing core module
cons: Couples ledger to unrelated code; harder to keep a single choke-point — rejected

chosen: A: new self-contained core/usage-ledger module + registry entry, opt-in
rationale: A dedicated module gives one clear append choke-point, isolated tests, and a clean extension surface for later slices, while the opt-in flag keeps it inert by default. Reusing the runtime-artifact-registry ensures the JSONL path is excluded from materialHash and treated as volatile/repairable so it never pollutes evidence.

preMortem.scenario: Later code writes the ledger via a second path, breaking completeness/hash-chain
preMortem.mitigation: Expose exactly ONE append function; keep file I/O private to writer.ts; smoke asserts there is a single exported write path and no other module writes the file
Validator rejects raw-content fields + a key/secret denylist; writer refuses to write on rejection; injection test must be rejected

preMortem.scenario: Ledger path pollutes materialHash / evidence freshness
preMortem.consequence: Gate hashes churn; evidence goes stale spuriously
preMortem.mitigation: Registry entry materialHash=exclude + volatile=true + repairableTrackedArtifact=true + ignorePatterns; smoke asserts the path classifies that way

preMortem.scenario: Opt-in flag defaults ON, so the writer runs unexpectedly
preMortem.mitigation: Flag default OFF; smoke asserts flag-off => no file created

preMortem.scenario: Record shape drifts from spec (stores totalTokens or wrong cache field names)
preMortem.consequence: Future slices inconsistent; cost accounting wrong
preMortem.mitigation: Validator enforces the spec shape and REJECTS stored totalTokens; types name the four cache-aware fields exactly; smoke checks field names + rejection

preMortem.trigger: previousRecordHash not read from last line
preMortem.mitigation: Writer reads the last record's recordHash and sets it as previousRecordHash; smoke appends multiple records and verifies the chain end-to-end
